group_scale_analytics.hypothesis: G128 chosen only as a historical reference point for cost accounting, not selected for future design.

arithmetic.current: For each output row o: d_o=sum_j sign(w_oj)*q_j in int32; output=round_F32(round_F32(float(d_o)*scale_o)*activation_scale_token).
arithmetic.grouped_hypothesis: For each row o: output=activation_scale_token*sum_g scale_og*sum_(j in group_g) sign(w_oj)*q_j, with an explicitly chosen floating reduction/rounding order.
arithmetic.consequence: A single post-dot row factor cannot represent independent groups. Integer multiply/add product count need not increase, but independent partial accumulators, scale loads/multiplies, group reduction and synchronization may increase latency. Group128 entails20/40/60 partial sums per row for K2560/5120/7680; native fusion may avoid intermediate tensors. This is not a measured latency multiplier.
arithmetic.unchanged_if_weights_fixed: Packed sign bits, current per-token activation codes/scale and nominal sign-times-A8 product count can stay unchanged if grouping changes scales alone. Historical R512 rotations need not and must not be silently combined.
arithmetic.excluded: GGUF metadata/alignment/other tensors, activation/KV/scratch/allocator, scale initial buffers, serialization staging, cache traffic and implementation-specific temporary group partial sums.
arithmetic.analytic_unit: One input vector independently through each of nine matrices; NOT one emitted token or server round. Encoder/catch-up/sample call and row counts differ.

primary_research.title: EAGLE-3: Scaling up Inference Acceleration of Large Language Models via Training-Time Test
primary_research.supports: Uses multi-layer target features, direct token loss and recurrent training-time feedback with appropriate attention masks. This motivates preserving native recurrence/masks and cautions against treating hidden-vector MSE as a universally suitable auxiliary.
primary_research.does_not_support: No evidence for current binary per-row scales, grouped-A8 speed, fixed-sign QAT sufficiency, or a validated early training predictor. Published speedups are not local baselines.

primary_research.title: DFlash: Block Diffusion for Flash Speculative Decoding
primary_research.supports: Parallel block drafting conditions on target features via KV injection. Position-dependent loss decay emphasizes earlier proposals; appendix contrasts uniform weighting. Offline precomputed features are supported in that architecture.
primary_research.does_not_support: No proof that its loss schedule, scaling or KV design transfers to the current recurrent binary drafter. No authorization to switch architecture. Its reported speedups are not comparable with this frozen local runtime.

primary_research.title: BitNet b1.58 2B4T Technical Report
primary_research.supports: Trains from scratch using ternary weights and per-token absmax8-bit activations, with architectural choices including subln and squared ReLU; exposes separate master versus inference weights.
primary_research.does_not_support: Does not demonstrate successful binary-sign conversion of this drafter, full-sign modern QAT readiness, row/group-scale choice, or that ternary native kernels equal current packed DP4A semantics. Ternary is not binary.

primary_research.title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
primary_research.supports: Independent groups of consecutive weights can reduce quantization error with extra metadata. Paper distinguishes memory-based speedups from computational reductions and explicitly leaves activation quantization outside its scope.
primary_research.does_not_support: Its group128 results/FP16 scales/zero-point overhead do not estimate binary/F32-group/A8 behavior or acceptance. Our byte arithmetic below uses our current geometry and F32 scales, not its bits-per-weight constants.
